BAY PROCEDURE Tacoma RV Center · Document Library CONCERN Lippert Ground Control 5th-wheel leveling: auto-level lifts the driver-side tires off the ground even though the coach was nearly level. MODEL Lippert Ground Control 343633 DATE 2026-10-09 WO# - PRIMARY Lippert Internal Tech Support - Electric Leveling Systems (Ground Control TT/2.0/3.0), page 1. VISUAL FLOWCHART Lippert Ground Control 5th-wheel leveling: auto-level lifts the driver-side tires off the ground even though the coach was nearly level. Run manual level. Front to back, then side to side. Then set the zero point with the touch pad off. FRONT five times, REAR five times, then press ENTER. Does auto-level still lift one side? Repeat the button sequence. That is the confirmed correction. YES NO BAY PROCEDURE Bay order · Tacoma RV Center WHAT THIS PATTERN USUALLY MEANS Auto-level that lifts one side of the coach is a zero-point calibration on Lippert Ground Control. Run manual level, then set zero point. Do not swap a level sensor and do not replace a harness. BAY ORDER (DO THIS FIRST) 1. Confirm the controller, jack, and touch pad plugs are seated. If a plug is loose, reseat it and retest auto-level. If the plugs are seated, go to manual level. 2. Run manual level. In manual mode, run the jacks until the trailer is level: level front to back, then side to side. When the coach is level, turn the touch pad off. 3. With the touch pad off, press and release FRONT five times, then press and release REAR five times. Press ENTER to store the zero point. If auto-level still lifts one side, repeat that button sequence. That is the confirmed correction. DO NOT - Do not swap a level sensor. - Do not replace a harness for an auto-level that lifts one side.
